title: India Retain Asian Games Women's Cricket Gold With Record 147-Run Win Over Sri Lanka
excerpt: Smriti Mandhana's 45-ball 79 — and a record 216 for 3 — powered India to a crushing 147-run victory over Sri Lanka in the final, the country's first gold of the 2026 Asian Games.
body:
• India defended their Asian Games women's cricket title with a crushing 147-run victory over Sri Lanka in the final at Nisshin, Aichi, on Tuesday — the country's first gold medal of the 2026 Games.
  • Smriti Mandhana struck a 45-ball 79, becoming the first woman cricketer to reach 11,000 international runs, as India posted 216 for 3 — the highest women's total in Asian Games history.
  • Sri Lanka were bundled out for 69 in 15.4 overs, their heaviest defeat in women's T20 internationals, with Deepti Sharma, Shafali Verma and Shree Charani sharing seven wickets between them.
  • Captain Harmanpreet Kaur said the win had "opened the gate" for India's medal campaign, with the squad targeting more golds in the days ahead.

NISSHIN, Japan — India crushed Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the women's Twenty20 final at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Tuesday, retaining their cricket gold in the most dominant final the competition has produced. Electing to bat in a rematch of the Hangzhou final, the defending champions piled up 216 for 3 at the Korogi Sports Park before their bowlers dismantled the Sri Lankan chase for just 69.

A record-breaking batting display

The tone was set in the first over, when Smriti Mandhana struck two boundaries off Sugandika Kumari. By the end of the powerplay India had raced to 67 without loss, and the assault never relented. Mandhana and Shafali Verma — fresh from Verma's unbeaten century in the semifinal win over Bangladesh — put on 99 for the opening wicket in 10 overs, dismantling the Sri Lankan attack with a mix of clean striking and audacious strokeplay.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=D25ne5ioBYw

Mandhana brought up her 37th T20 international half-century and, in the process, became the first woman cricketer to reach 11,000 runs in international cricket. Her 45-ball 79 featured seven sixes and five fours and seemed destined for a hundred until she holed out to deep backward square attempting her eighth maximum.

Verma fell for a brisk 48 off 29 balls, top-edging a reverse sweep off Chamudi Praboda, and Harmanpreet Kaur contributed 19 off 17 before falling to Kavisha Dilhari. But Richa Ghosh provided the late fireworks, blasting an unbeaten 49 off just 22 balls to carry India well past 200. The innings featured 18 fours and 13 sixes — a new benchmark for women's cricket at the Asian Games.

Ruthless with the ball

Chasing 217 for gold was always beyond Sri Lanka, and India's bowlers made sure the contest ended early. Verma returned with the ball to strike in consecutive overs with her off-spin, removing Imesha Dulani and Hasini Perera, before the spinners closed ranks. Sri Lanka's faint hopes rested on captain Chamari Athapaththu, but when she miscued Deepti Sharma to depart for 27, the innings folded. Sri Lanka were all out for 69 in 15.4 overs — their heaviest defeat in women's T20 internationals, eclipsing the 132-run loss to Australia in 2019.

"It was good to see Smriti and Shafali give us a big start again. We're really happy that we have opened the gate now, and hopefully we'll see many more golds coming up."

— Harmanpreet Kaur, India captain

Back-to-back titles, and a statement of intent

The victory gives India consecutive Asian Games cricket golds, and the margin — 147 runs, India's largest in women's T20 internationals — underlines how far ahead of the Asian field this side now sits. Pakistan took the bronze, beating Bangladesh in the third-place playoff. For a squad that has also lifted the Asia Cup in recent months, as Harmanpreet noted, the batters "have been outstanding in the last two tournaments — Asia Cup and Asian Games — and they've been taking responsibility."

What comes next

For India, the gold is the first of what the contingent hopes will be many in Nagoya, and it lands at a useful moment: the women's game in India is drawing record audiences and investment, and a title defended this emphatically only strengthens the case for more. The players now scatter back to domestic and franchise commitments, but the core of this squad will be the spine of India's challenge at the next global tournaments. On this evidence, the chasing pack in Asia has serious catching up to do.

nri_angle: A second straight Asian Games gold — and India's first medal of the 2026 Games — gives the global Indian diaspora a marquee win to rally around, with Mandhana's record 11,000 international runs adding a historic individual milestone.
